articles.title: Fantasy Football Rankings: Hayden Winks' WR Blueprint for Week 2
articles.summary: Fantasy football analyst Hayden Winks drops the WR Blueprint for Week 2.
articles.body:
The Blueprint is my weekly column and basically every thing that I use to build out the most accurate rankings I can. There will be a RB column , this WR column and a combination column on the onesie positions . You will find film notes and endless charts. Maybe enough charts to stress test the Yahoo website. I kid.

It's impossible to get every rankings thoroughly by Thursday Night Football, so be sure to keep checking in on these columns through Sunday morning. As always, my full rankings at every position are available .

Note: Total-yardage projections are based on betting markets.

1. Puka Nacua (vs. NYG) - 85.5 proj. receiving yards

Matthew Stafford was brutal in Week 1. He wasn't seeing things well and made life way harder than needed. That's the outlier game, and even then, Nacua was the WR11 in expected half-PPR points (13.0) despite not finishing the game with starters on the field.

This week's matchup is far more normal. First, it's in the United States. Second, it's not a divisional opponent from the same coaching tree. Third, the Giants' starting CBs are in the midst of tryouts for snaps. It's a cupcake matchup for Nacua, who did something in Week 1 that wasn't the case in 2025 when he was the clear-cut WR1 overall in fantasy: play in 1-WR set snaps at the goal line. That can't be understated after Davante Adams goal-line-faded his way to a top-10 fantasy season in 2025 solely off that role.

2. Amon-Ra St. Brown (at BUF) - 79.5 proj. receiving yards

The Sun God had the best usage of any WR in Week 1, according to my expected half-PPR points model (20.8). New OC Drew Petzig typically highlights a slot/TE type to run his offense through, and that's absolutely ARSB this year. Meanwhile, the Lions' OL and DBs are beat up. They're missing their starting LG, C and RT on offense, and both safeties and possibly a starting CB on defense. Detroit will have to pass more because of that, and Jared Goff has already been the QB2 in passing yards in 3-street seasons.

The matchup is a very good one, too. The Lions are projected for 25.0 points (eighth) as 4.5-point dogs in Buffalo. The Bills have a solid CB1 in Christian Benford , but he'll be tasked with Jameson Williams as a boundary player, while St. Brown has the best individual matchup. They've struggled against slot types recently, to the point that St. Brown has a case to be the WR1 overall in Week 2.

3. Jaxon Smith-Njigba (at ARI) - 81.5 proj. receiving yards

The drop off from Sam Darnold to Drew Lock is real, but Lock is at least a gunslinger who will give his top guys chances down the field. JSN saved his week one with a hitch against the blitz, where he outran everyone despite a mediocre 40-yard dash time. He still had WR4 expected half-PPR points (17.8) with Lock in a clear win.

This week, the Seahawks are slight favorites with a 22.5-point team total (18th) in Arizona . That defense was surprisingly solid in Week 1 against the Chargers, showing nice communication in zone coverage. They don't have a star CB1, however, and Ladd McConkey was gashing them for chunk plays before his hospital-ball rib injury. JSN has also been extremely efficient in this exact matchup historically:

4. Justin Jefferson (at CHI) - 77.5 proj. receiving yards

In 54 games since 2022 without J.J. McCarthy , Jefferson is the WR3 on WR7 usage, averaging 95 YPG and 107 air yards per game. In six games with Carson Wentz , Jefferson is the WR4 on WR7 usage, averaging 95 YPG and 105 air yards per game. In other words, Wentz has been generally as good at getting Jefferson the ball as the rest of the Vikings QBs recently.

The Bears were a mess in Week 1 with SCB Kyler Gordon and S Coby Bryant sidelined. Jalen Coker finished as the WR1 overall, while Tetairoa McMillan had 119 air yards. This was the same thing that happened in 2025, when the Bears allowed the second-most fantasy points to WRs. With DC Dennis Allen, they're going to live and die with their man coverage ability. They had the second-highest man coverage rate of Week 1. Long story short, this is a great spot. The Vikings are projected for 22.0 points (19th) in projected negative game script as slight road dogs.

5. Ja'Marr Chase (at HOU) - 75.5 proj. receiving yards

Chase had the rare dud with Joe Burrow healthy. There were some slight differences in the offense, but nothing too drastic. The Bengals were third in neutral pass rate still. Chase had a fade to the goal line that went incomplete and did stumble at the top of an in-cut on another target, so perhaps he's still working back from his hyperextended knee in camp. He looked fast in a straight line, caught a screen and hit a toe-tapper on the sideline. Things will even out.

The Texans obviously are a horrible draw for Week 2. The Bengals only project for 21.75 points (20th) in Houston , who have two great CBs to match up with both WRs. In 2025, the Texans were fifth-best against fantasy WRs, allowing just 200 total passing yards to all positions. Chase did face the Texans in Week 10 of 2023 and he hung 5-124-1 on six targets on them, for what it's worth.

6. CeeDee Lamb (vs. WAS) - 75.5 proj. receiving yards

Lamb had a solid debut against the Giants, who bled out the clock and limited the Cowboys offense to just 34 dropbacks and 52 plays. Lamb had his signature 27% target share and 13.4 expected half-PPR points (WR10), which lines up with his splits next to George Pickens from 2025. Lamb averaged 89 receiving yards per game on a 26% target share, if we remove his two injured games. He was the WR8 on WR6 usage, with the only real difference being he scored 0.25 touchdowns per game rather than his baseline of 0.37.

The Commanders are running a new chaotic defense, but their secondary remains in pretty tough shape. Mike Sainristil struggled in the opener, and Lamb has averaged 75 yards on 6.9 receptions in seven games against the Commanders since 2022. He had a 5-110-1 game against them just last year. It's a great spot for Lamb. Dallas has a 27.5-point team total (fifth) at home.

7. George Pickens (vs. WAS) - 62.5 proj. receiving yards

Pickens had a poor Week 1 outing, just as he did in 2025 before lighting up the league the rest of the way. Pickens dropped an in-cut and downfield sideline go ball, and that was the difference. At the same time, Pickens drew a 41-yard DPI on third down and came away with three underneath catches on strong route running. There's no reason to change our perspective out of Week 1. He had 104 air yards and a 20% target share and 90% route rate. In 14 games with Lamb, Pickens is the WR14 on WR15 usage on a 22% target share, while running less hot than usual on TDs. He's a low-end WR1.

The matchup with the Commanders is a great one. The Cowboys are fifth in projected points (27.5) while at home, and the Commanders allowed splash plays to Dontayvion Wicks (twice), Devonta Smith and Dallas Goedert last week.

8. DJ Moore (vs. DET) - 63.5 proj. receiving yards

Moore had a very promising debut, beyond just scoring 18.5-half PPR points. His 43-yard TD was out of structure because Josh Allen is a wizard, but he also had a slot target and multiple downfield shots. He drew a 47-yard DPI in the end zone off an under-center play action and another defensive holding down the field, then was given two other prayer shots down the field. That all led to 158 air yards (WR3).

The Bills project for the most points of Week 2, and the Lions secondary is extremely beat up. Their top two safeties are out, and CB2 DJ Reed (foot) is questionable. Even last year, the Lions allowed the third-most fantasy points to WRs. Then they were lit up by WRs Chris Olave and Devaughn Vele down the field in Week 2, and that's exactly where Moore is going to operate in this offense. It's as tasty of a matchup as he'll get all year.

9. Chris Olave (at BAL) - 74.5 proj. receiving yards

Olave has 10 games with Tyler Shough now. He's the WR4 (15.9 half-PPR points) on WR7 usage in them, averaging 91 yards on 139 air yards and 9.8 targets per game. This is an elite role at least until Jordyn Tyson comes back in the mix. The Saints were first in neutral pace in 2025 and followed that up in Week 1, when the offense was lighting up the Lions in the second half and overtime. They ran 86 plays!!!

This matchup is the polar opposite. The Ravens defense was flying around the field in Week 1 with star players littered in the secondary. He'll likely see a ton of CB1 Nate Wiggins , who has the speed to match with Olave down the field. They also have new HC Jesse Minter to use superstar S Kyle Hamilton as they see fit. They allowed -0.44 EPA per dropback last week. Because of this potentially great defense, the Saints only project for 19.0 points (27th). Olave also popped up with a hamstring injury on Thursday; something to monitor.

10. Garrett Wilson (vs. GB) - 64.5 proj. receiving yards

The Jets took care of business against the Titans in Week 1. Wilson and Geno Smith looked great on film, and the pass game flowed through the former still. He had another 30% target share, which will lead to even bigger games when they're playing in negative game script.

The Packers are a great matchup for Wilson. Green Bay 's offense can't run the ball, and their pass-game looks extremely explosive. They could put up points in a hurry or punt the ball quickly, leading to more plays for the Jets, who are 3.5-point dogs at home. Green Bay's defense is also a weakness. They're sixth-worst in EPA per dropback and second-worst in sack rate since Week 15 of last year when Micah Parsons went down.

11. Mike Evans (vs. MIA) - 48.5 proj. receiving yards

Unc still got it. Evans looked great in a slightly altered role in his Week 1 debut against a loaded secondary. The Niners got him on a few quick out routes, then gave him a signature end-zone fade for a TD. It was a clean 21% target share, and those targets will be very efficient in this offense. Beyond that, De'Zhaun Stribling's snaps will be replaced by low-volume clear-out WR Demarcus Robinson and George Kittle didn't look like himself on tape. It's a great spot all around.

This week's matchup does not get any easier. The 49ers are second in projected points (29.0) against the Dolphins, who have the youngest defense in the NFL by far. They're trotting out a rookie CB, and Chris Johnson was lit up for double-digit targets in the opener. Expect Evans to see bust CB1 JuJu Brents plenty. BBQ chicken.

12. Malik Nabers (at LAR) - 65.5 proj. receiving yards

Nabers ran a route on 71% of dropbacks in his return from multiple knee surgeries, leading to an elite 31% target share, 103 air yards and WR14 expected half-PPR points. On tape, Nabers looked explosive in a straight line and he still was able to make a few impressive cuts after the catch. He did slip three times at the top of his route while breaking left and back towards the ball. We can live with that as he ramps back up over the next month or so. In the meantime, Nabers' role and quality of play are absolutely worth starting, even if he's not quite in the top 12 yet. He's on the path of getting there by the time fantasy matchups have real dollars at stake.

The Rams have stars in the secondary, but they at least won't have Myles Garrett and potentially won't have Aaron Donald yet. If the Rams offense returns to form back in the United States, then Nabers should have plenty of targets in a more favorable game script. The Giants are 7-point dogs with a 20.75-point team total.

13. DeVonta Smith (at TEN) - 60.5 proj. receiving yards

The Eagles had some issues on the ground, but they hit chunk plays in the air and did enough schematically against a unique Commanders defense to give us confidence with Smith and Jalen Hurts . Smith is going to be boom-bust, as they seemed to tailor their manufactured touches to first-round slot Makai Lemon instead. Smith still had a 27% target share with a 13.2 average depth of target, a nice sweet spot in my opinion. His -12.2% completion percentage over expectation will normalize, and he should be a good WR2 in fantasy on average.

The matchup is a nice one here. The Titans couldn't stop the Jets in Week 1, and the Eagles are projected for 23.25 points (14th) despite being on the road. The Titans' top outside CBs are pretty volatile, Alontae Taylor (who should be a slot CB imo) and Cor'Dale Flott and Smith is one of the best cross-over route runners in the league.

14. Christian Watson (at NYJ) - 60.5 proj. receiving yards

Green Bay's OL can't run block, and their RBs can't hit the hole either. They opted to be eighth in neutral pass rate (60%) and second in neutral pace instead. They've been bottom in each category since Josh Jacobs arrived years ago. It's a big deal. Beyond that, the Packers didn't rotate their WRs much. Watson and Matthew Golden are near full-time players, soaking up 20% and 30% of the targets, respectively. Watson hit the gas on an in-cut for an 81-yarder, then had a manufactured target at the goal line for a second score. It all led to WR12 expected half-PPR points in Week 1. He's a model breaker on top of that.

The matchup is a very clean one. The Jets offense looked competent, and their defense is missing star players in the secondary. Watson will face off with boom-bust CBs AZ Thomas and Brandon Stephens on the perimeter. It doesn't look like the Jets will have S Minkah Fitzpatrick or EDGE Joseph Ossai either. The Packers are projected for 24.0 points (13th).

15. Emeka Egbuka (vs. CLE) - 54.5 proj. receiving yards

Egbuka was fine in Week 1 (WR33 on WR36 usage), but the film was quite promising. He looked healthy on his toe and was very clearly more athletic than Chris Godwin Jr., who was used as a physical power slot underneath. Egbuka ran more digs and had all of the fun motion plays. They leaked him often, had him run through the B gap a couple of times and was targeted deep downfield on a motion-wheel. It was very Rams-coded (bullish). When Baker Mayfield feels less skittish, then Egbuka should have big games ahead.

The Browns had issues with the Jaguars in Week 1, only pressuring that mediocre OL on four dropbacks. They allowed the third-most fantasy points to WRs. Parker Washington , who plays the same role in the same coaching tree, had multiple explosives, including a corner route TD from the slot. Ebguka will see some CB1 Denzel Ward , but it will not be the entire time at all. Tampa Bay has a 25.0-point team total (ninth). It's a good matchup.

16. Parker Washington (at DEN) - 55.5 proj. receiving yards

Since Week 7 of last year, Washington is the WR14 on WR12 usage on a per-game basis. That's a 23% target share on a quality offense.

Washington ran a route on 72% of dropbacks, which was a bit lower than expected. He played almost all of the 3-WR sets, splitting time between Z and the slot. He rotated in the non 3-WR set snaps, however, losing some playing time to rookie WR Josh Cameron and others. That said, he's clearly the top target whenever he's out there. Washington led with an elite 29% target share and 102 air yards. He roasted a SCB for a man-coverage corner route TD and had multiple crossing-route wins. He added a one-handed grab on a quick out for good measure. It all led to a WR10 start on WR29 usage in a blowout win.

The matchup is far more difficult this week. The Jaguars are on the road, projecting for 21.5 points (20th) in Denver . Since 2025, the Broncos have been the best defense against fantasy WRs when adjusting for schedule. He won't see much of CB1 Patrick Surtain at least, but CB2 Riley Moss and SCB Ja'Quan McMillan are above average in their roles … but as I pull up the Broncos' box scores, I find that the receiver who had the best fantasy game against them was Mr. Washington himself (6-145-1 on 10 targets in Week 16).

17. Tetairoa McMillan (at ATL) - 57.5 proj. receiving yards

McMillan was just fine in Week 1. He ran a couple of great routes and remains an awesome big-body target in clutch situations. His WR22 expected points were nothing to sneeze at, but McMillan did look a step slower on some of the crossing and go routes versus last year, if we want to over analyze it.

He should be more physical at the catch point and in after-catch situations, but the real Week 1 takeaway is the gap between McMillan and Coker was too large in drafts. That mostly means Coker is flying up rest-of-season rankings than McMillan is tanking. However, McMillan is the WR28 on WR35 usage in eight games since Jalen Coker was a full-time player in Week 12 of last year. Their target shares are Coker, 23% and McMillan, 22%.

McMillan and Coker both play inside and out, but McMillan will generally get the top corner when all else is equal. The Falcons have a good one in A.J. Terrell here. That didn't stop McMillan from a monster 8-130-2 outing the last time they faced off. That was the most fantasy points Atlanta allowed all year.

18. Jaylen Waddle (vs. JAX) - 52.5 proj. receiving yards

Waddle flopped in Week 1. He had an 11% target share and 13 air yards. Come on!!! The potential long-term thorn here could be second-year WR Pat Bryant 's 22% target share. If there are three real weapons at WR, it's always harder to make the math work.

It's shocking to see Waddle's floor be so low, but the good news, if any, is the tape showed a lot more schemed-up opportunities for him than what the box score showed. Bo Nix turned down a swing pass, corner route and pick-wheel in the first half alone. They gave him a route out of the backfield, a third-and-4 choice route, a screen, plenty of switch releases, work out of the slot (59% of snaps), a third-and-7 slant (dropped) and more. The game plan seemed to prioritize Waddle a lot more than Nix allowed. It was more of a QB and C/RB/TE blocking thing than a scheme thing to me. The Broncos were first in neutral pass rate (72%), so the uptick in routes for Waddle should be a real thing.

We'll learn more about his availability (ribs) later in the week.

20. Terry McLaurin (at DAL) - 53.5 proj. receiving yards

McLaurin was predictably shut down by Eagles DC Vic Fangio and elite CB1 Quinyon Mitchell . Even with that dud, McLaurin is the WR14 on WR29 usage in games with Jayden Daniels . The top end of that outcome is very unlikely to repeat after running pure on touchdowns in 2024, but let's not panic here.

Especially not this week. The Cowboys struggled with communication in Week 1 against the Giants, to the point Jaxson Dart had a +0.71 EPA per dropback and Week 1 high 71% success rate. Since 2024, the Cowboys are allowing the most fantasy points to WRs when adjusting for schedule. McLaurin has had two big games within that:

21. Tee Higgins (at HOU) - 55.5 proj. receiving yards

Higgins had a wild 19.5 average depth of target on his six targets in Week 1, leading to an elite 117 air yards. Some of it was performative under-center heaves from Joe Burrow, but those looks are very valuable and I'd guess the Bengals keep up their under-center play-action looks as a third pitch in the offense. Burrow had a 14.3 aDOT under center versus a 6.3 aDOT in the gun on a half second quicker time to throw. Higgins is the WR16 on WR24 usage since 2025 with Burrow in the lineup, and he was even better than that in 2024. Nothing has really changed.

Unfortunately, this is a difficult spot. Burrow seems a bit banged up, and the Texans were the fifth-best defense against fantasy WRs last year with a secondary that all could make the Pro Bowl. Cincy's team total is lower than usual at 22.0 points (19th).

22. Davante Adams (vs. NYG) - 44.5 proj. receiving yards

23. Matthew Golden (at NYJ) - 49.5 proj. receiving yards

24. Jameson Williams (at BUF) - 57.5 proj. receiving yards

Williams will have a very boom-bust role with Sam LaPorta healthy. In nine games since 2025 with LaPorta available, Williams is the WR43 on WR54 usage in half PPR, even though he's averaged 10.0 YPT in that sample. Williams' average depth of target climbs to 14.8 yards downfield as the primary clear out player. That was his role in Week 1, when he came up close to empty on 127 air yards (!!!) and 13.9 expected half-PPR points (WR7). There will be WR50 weeks. There will be WR5 weeks. They'll just be hard to predict before the week.

Williams' individual matchup is solid. The Lions are projected for 25.0 points and are set up in more pass-heavy script as road dogs. The Lions are missing 3-of-5 OL starters and multiple DBs, so don't be surprised if Goff drops back a ton. Jamo will face shadow CB1 Christian Benford on the perimeter and he had an up-and-down game against Nico Collins in Week 1, traveling with him on each side of the field.

25. DK Metcalf (at NE) - 50.5 proj. receiving yards

Metcalf had excellent usage in Week 1. He was the WR6 in expected half-PPR points (15.0) on 204 air yards and a 27% target share. It helped that the Steelers were fifth in neutral pass rate (66%) in new HC Mike McCarthy's debut, far higher than last year's 54%. Was it effective? Nope. He had a drop over the middle, an OPI on an out route and a few near completions way down the field. We'll see if the Steelers felt like last week's game plan holds as September rolls on, but this was a far more downfield role (20.4 average depth of target) for their WR1.

The matchup is a difficult one. The Patriots have elite CB1 Christian Gonzalez, who has the size and speed to match up with Metcalf. New England allowed just 201 YPG through the air in 2025. He had 35 yards in this matchup in Week 3 of last year, too. Pittsburgh has things to work on, and the betting markets agree, as they have the 29th team total of Week 2 (18.0).

26. Drake London (vs. CAR) - 56.5 proj. receiving yards

Don't read too much into the Falcons' Week 1 brutal start, unless Cooper Rush continues to start. We'll learn more later in the week. This assumes it's Rush again.

The bigger thing to note from Week 1 was the minor changes in the offense. London's slot rate fell from 34% last year to 16% in Week 1. He's an excellent big slot, so losing some of that work will hurt the margins.

27. Rome Odunze (vs. MIN) - 39.5 proj. receiving yards

28. Jalen Coker (at ATL) - 50.5 proj. receiving yards

Jalen Coker started and played 82% snaps in Week 12 of last year. In eight games since then, he's the WR11 on WR27 usage in half PPR. He's running really hot, but the usage is real and he is undeniably a good player. Without much depth in Carolina, he might be a fantasy WR3.

29. Luther Burden (vs. MIN) - 51.5 proj. receiving yards

30. Rashee Rice (vs. IND) - 53.5 proj. receiving yards

Rice scored a 13-yard touchdown, bouncing off two defenders on a 1-on-1 "screen." He only had six receiving yards on 26 non-screen routes, however. The Chiefs offense also flipped, as expected. They had a 58% neutral pass rate over the past three seasons, then in Week 1 with Kenneth Walker dominating, the Chiefs had a 48% neutral pass rate. That'll hurt Rice' PPR-scam ability. The good news is the pass game remained quite dink-and-dunk, but it's still unclear just how healthy Rice is after a second knee surgery this offseason. He looked just fine to me. His 3.3 expected half-PPR points (WR88) and 8% target share has to be nerve-racking for Round 3 drafters, though (not me).

The Colts were gashed in Week 1, but they did play the most man coverage (56%) and that's exactly what gives Rice issues. 2025 third-round SCB Justin Walley made his debut after injury last week, and it didn't go well. The individual matchup is decent, but Rice will have to buck his trend of being a total non-factor against man. The Chiefs are projected for 26.5 points (sixth) at home.

31. Deebo Samuel (vs. MIA) - 35.5 proj. receiving yards

33. Stefon Diggs (at DAL) - 46.5 proj. receiving yards

34. Alec Pierce (at KC) - 45.5 proj. receiving yards

35. Chris Godwin Jr. (vs. CLE) - 47.5 proj. receiving yards

Godwin is out of his prime on tape. He did absolutely yeet a couple of Bengals tacklers after the catch with grown-man strength, but his speed is officially lackluster, as it was last season. He was targeted four times, three of which were behind the line of scrimmage. Emeka Egbuka was given more at-snap motion responsibilities as the primary intermediate target on the team. Godwin had the negative game script last week, yet mustered just a 15% target share. He's a WR4 bench stash while everyone is healthy. He could be a mid-volume, red-zone threat to wind down his career.

36. Jayden Reed (at NYJ) - 37.5 proj. receiving yards

articles.title: Saints news: Tyler Shough gets 'poor man's Josh Allen' comparison from DC
articles.summary: Tyler Shough is only entering the second game of his second NFL season, but he’s already drawing comparisons to one of the league’s biggest superstars. Balti...
articles.body:
Tyler Shough is only entering the second game of his second NFL season, but he's already drawing comparisons to one of the league's biggest superstars.

Baltimore Ravens defensive coordinator Anthony Weaver said Thursday that Shough reminds him of a "poor man's Josh Allen ," pointing specifically to the New Orleans Saints quarterback's arm strength and mobility.

Weaver knows firsthand what Shough can do. While serving as Miami 's defensive coordinator last season, Weaver watched Shough throw for 239 yards and two touchdowns against the Dolphins.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Now Shough looks considerably more comfortable. The 26-year-old opened his second season by completing 35 of 56 passes for a career-high 410 yards, three touchdowns and two interceptions in New Orleans ' 31-30 overtime loss to Detroit . New Orleans fell behind 21-0 before Shough and the offense finally came alive . The Saints scored on five of their final six possessions and eventually forced overtime before falling short on a two-point conversion attempt.

That's the version of Shough that should have Saints fans excited. Nobody is putting him in Allen's class after one 400-yard performance. Allen himself needed time before developing into one of the NFL's premier quarterbacks.

Shough has plenty of time to establish his own identity in Kellen Moore's offense. New Orleans isn't loaded with the type of roster that will make life easy for its young quarterback, either. That makes Shough's development one of the most important storylines surrounding the Saints this season.

Baltimore will provide another difficult test Sunday. If Shough can follow his Week 1 performance with another impressive showing against Weaver's defense, that "poor man's Josh Allen " comparison might start sounding a little more complimentary.

articles.title: RJ Harvey returns to practice Thursday
articles.summary: Broncos RB RJ Harvey back on practice field after a DNP Wednesday
articles.body:
Denver Broncos RB RJ Harvey (hamstring) was limited during practice Thursday, Sept. 17.

Why It Matters: Harvey is making progress in his recovery, but fantasy players will know more about his Week 2 status after the final practice of the week. He received seven touches in the opener and will probably see a similar workload if active. He can be a possible flex option in some deeper fantasy leagues.

articles.title: How Novak Djokovic performed in his first-ever China Open as he announces 2026 return
articles.summary: Novak Djokovic is set to compete at the China Open for the first time in 11 years. With six China Open titles to his name,...
articles.body:
Novak Djokovic is set to compete at the China Open for the first time in 11 years.

With six China Open titles to his name, Djokovic is the most successful male player in tournament history.

The Serbian superstar, who recently exited the ATP top 10 after losing in the US Open first round, confirmed his participation in the 2026 event in a social media video posted on Wednesday.

Djokovic made his first-ever appearance at the Beijing-based event in 2009.

How did the tennis icon perform on his debut?

Novak Djokovic won the China Open on debut

Djokovic entered the 2009 China Open as the second seed, behind only Rafael Nadal.

The Serb handled his first two rounds with ease, defeating Victor Hanescu and compatriot Viktor Troicki in straight sets.

He then survived a scare against Fernando Verdasco in the quarter-finals, triumphing 6-3, 1-6, 6-1 in the Chinese capital.

Djokovic defeated Robin Soderling 6-3, 6-3 in the semi-finals, setting up a clash with 2014 US Open champion Marin Cilic.

Cilic, the eighth-seeded wildcard entry, stunned top seed Rafael Nadal in the semi-finals.

Djokovic proved too strong for the Croatian, claiming his first China Open title with a 6-2, 7-6 victory.

Djokovic went on to claim six China Open titles in seven years, including four in a row between 2012 and 2015.

2009: defeated Marin Cilic in the final, 6–2, 7–6

2010: defeated David Ferrer in the final, 6–2, 6–4

2012: defeated Jo-Wilfried Tsonga in the final, 7–6, 6–2

2013: defeated Rafael Nadal in the final, 6–3, 6–4

2014: defeated Tomas Berdych in the final, 6–0, 6–2

2015: defeated Rafael Nadal in the final, 6–2, 6–2

What did Novak Djokovic say ahead of winning the 2015 China Open?

In 2015, Only Rafael Nadal stood in the way of Novak Djokovic winning a sixth China Open title.

Prior to the final in Beijing, Djokovic described his record in China as one of his greatest accomplishments as a tennis player.

"This is right at the top, one of the best achievements I've had in my career," Djokovic stated prior to playing Nadal.

"Every time I keep coming back, I have these positive, great memories from the success, the great performances I had on the centre court, support, just overall feel is very positive.

Djokovic defeated Nadal in emphatic fashion, triumphing 6-2, 6-2.

Djokovic has only lost one match at the China Open : Novak and Djordje Djokovic were beaten by Vasek Pospisil and Jack Sock in the 2015 men's doubles event.

articles.title: Jonathan Bale grabs lead at 101st Crump Memorial
articles.summary: Jonathan Bale shot a 1-over-par 71 to take the lead at the 101st George Arthur Crump Memorial at Pine Valley.
articles.body:
Jonathan Bale made three birdies on the back nine and shot a 1-over par 71 in the first round of stroke-play qualifying of the 101st annual George Arthur Crump Memorial Tournament at Pine Valley.

Bale, a resident of Jupiter, Florida, leads a logjam of players two strokes off the pace that includes Chadd Slutzky of Deer Park, Illinois, Drew Kittleson of Scottsdale, Arizona, Gregor Orlando of Haverford, Pennsylvania, Andrew Bailey of Shaker Heights, Ohio, U.S. Walker Cupper Stewart Hagestad of Hermosa Beach, California, Chris Wheeler of Lewisville, Texas, and Chad Wilfong of Charlotte, North Carolina. Defending champion Bobby Wyatt has his work cut out to make match play after opening with 77.

A trio of past senior champions lead the Senior Division at 74. Michael McCoy of Norwalk, Iowa, Jamie Slonis of Sewell, New Jersey, and Tommy Brennan of Covington, Louisiana finished two strokes better than defending senior champion Bob Royak of Alpharetta, Georgia.

The Open division has 78 players competing for 48 spots in match play while 21 senior players are contending for 16 spots.

The Crump Cup is arguably the premier mid-amateur tournament in the United States. Pine Valley is ranked second in the latest Golfweek's Best Classic Courses list.

Pine Valley Golf Club will not be open to the public for Sunday's final match of the 2026 Crump Memorial Tournament as had been the case pre-COVID.
